title: Mecz i drużyna
note: A2 liść · games, exercise and watching — the being-outdoors half (landscape, walking kit) went to a2_nature2 instead; spacer stayed here as the exercise word it actually is. a1_freetime already owns sport, piłka nożna, tenis, pływanie, bieganie, siłownia, hobby, muzyka, grać, gra, zabawa, drużyna, mecz, ćwiczyć and more — those are ANCHORS here, never re-taught (siłownia, drużyna and ćwiczyć were on the candidate list and were dropped once check_new.py confirmed them already live). jeździć is FENCED to a2_chodzic and does not appear anywhere in this pack, not even inside a sentence. This pack teaches 12 new words: piłka (the ball itself — distinct from the already-known compound piłka nożna), bramka, remis, medal, stadion, zawody, kibic, trener, spacer as nouns, plus biegać, wygrywać, przegrywać as verbs. Two watch-outs flagged deliberately: zawody (plural, the sports-competition word) sits right next to the already-taught zawód (singular, profession/career) — different word, easy to blur, called out in an explain note. oglądam/oglądać was already taught in the grammar pack a2_shopping_func as 'I'm looking, I'm browsing' (the shop-counter sense); this pack reuses the same verb in its central meaning, 'I watch', for Jutro oglądam zawody — same word, wider but consistent sense, not a false-friend swap, flagged here per the homograph-trap rule rather than let it pass silently. wynik (result, taught in leaf_ideas_a1) already covers 'score' too, but no sentence forces it in, so it stays an unused-but-available anchor. Imperfective only; no virile (masculine-personal) plural forms are used anywhere (kibice, sportowcy, grali etc. are all avoided) to keep this a vocabulary unit, not a grammar cliff.

sentences.explain: spacer is a masculine thing-word, so na spacer does not change it at all — unlike do parku, na spacer stays exactly as you see it.

sentences.en: I run in the park every day.
sentences.explain: biegam is built like mam and czytam — the -am family. You already know the noun bieganie (running); this is the verb it comes from.

sentences.en: Yesterday I ran in the morning.
sentences.explain: Regular imperfective past, same pattern as czytałem, robiłem — swap the -ć for -łem.

sentences.en: The team is winning the match.
sentences.explain: mecz does not change here — a masculine thing-word looks the same as subject and as object.

sentences.en: The team is losing the match.

sentences.explain: Saying what someone is puts the noun in the instrumental: kibic becomes kibicem, the same -em you already use in kelnerem and bratem.
zawody only exists as a plural, like wakacje — so the verb is są, never jest. Don't confuse it with zawód (a job/profession), a different word you already know.
oglądam is the same word from the shop counter (tylko oglądam, I'm just browsing) — its plain meaning is simply 'I watch/look at', which is exactly what it does here.
Not piłka nożna (football) here — just piłka, the object itself. Feminine -a becomes -ę as the object of mam, same as gitara → gitarę.

sentences.en: There was a goal in the park.
sentences.explain: This była announces that something existed in a place — the same existential pattern as w parku był staw, just in the past.
